title: AppSec Framework configuration (appsec.yaml)
description: Configuration for the appsec CLI. The Go parser is the runtime authority; this schema exists for editor completion and CI validation, and a conformance test asserts the two agree on a corpus of valid and invalid documents.

apiVersion.description: Configuration contract version. Required from the first release so that adding it later cannot invalidate existing files.

baseURL.description: Root of the application under assessment. Its origin is always in scope. Must not embed credentials.

include.description: Additional allowed endpoints. Scope is an allowlist; nothing outside it is contacted.

allowPrivateAddresses.description: Permit loopback and RFC1918 addresses. Required for a local target; cloud metadata addresses stay denied regardless.

profile.description: Safety profile. Strictly ordered; never escalates implicitly.

authorizeIntrusive.description: Required for the intrusive profile. Selecting a profile is not by itself authorization to use it.

excludeOperations.description: Operation ids that must never be exercised, e.g. "POST /orders".

excludeAuthEndpoints.description: Skip routes that look like authentication. Sweeping these can lock real accounts. Defaults to true.

identities.description: Security principals AppSec Framework may act as. A credential is never written here: only a reference to an environment variable or a file. M1 uses the first identity as the authenticated control; choosing between identities is an M2 concern.

id.description: Stable identity name used in the coverage ledger and reports. "anonymous" is reserved for the built-in credential-free identity.

type.description: bearer sends Authorization: Bearer <credential>. apiKey sends a configured header. OAuth2, OIDC, browser login and cookie-session flows are not supported.

header.description: Header carrying the credential, for the apiKey type. Validated as an RFC 9110 field name. Headers controlling message framing, the connection, or the tool's identifiability are refused.

valuePrefix.description: Prepended to the credential for the apiKey type, e.g. "Token ".

credential.description: Where the secret is read from. Exactly one of env or file. A literal credential value is deliberately not accepted.

file.description: File whose contents are the credential. Whitespace is trimmed.

liveness.description: A safe, authentication-requiring operation probed to establish whether the identity is still usable. Without one, a credential expiring mid-run cannot be detected.

method.description: Defaults to GET. A canary runs repeatedly, so it must be a safe method.

path.description: Resolved against target.baseURL and subject to the scope policy.

expectStatus.description: Statuses meaning the identity is still good. Empty means any 2xx.

resources.description: Concrete resources known to belong to an identity, used to test whether a non-owner can reach or change them. A fixture is what makes a cross-owner probe meaningful: without one, addressing /api/orders/{orderId} means inventing an identifier and reading a 404 that says nothing about authorization.

id.description: Stable fixture name used in the coverage ledger and reports.

type.description: Logical label such as "order". Descriptive only; nothing branches on it.

owner.description: The identities[].id that owns this resource.

crossOwnerAccess.description: Required. "denied" means non-owners must not reach the resource, which is the boundary a BOLA check tests. "allowed" means the resource is legitimately shared, so a non-owner reaching it is expected and is never a finding.

values.description: Values that fill the operation's declared parameters, keyed by parameter name. Each fills exactly one path segment and may not contain a path separator, a query or fragment delimiter, an authority delimiter, a percent sign or a control character.

operations.description: Optional allowlist of operation ids ("GET /api/orders/{orderId}"). Empty means every operation whose required path parameters this fixture can fill.

nonOwners.description: Optional allowlist of identities that probe this fixture. Empty means every configured identity except the owner.

mutation.description: Enables cross-owner write testing. Writes require the intrusive profile and explicit authorizeIntrusive, and a write is confirmed only by re-reading as the owner: an HTTP success never confirms one.

values.description: Explicit field/value pairs sent as a JSON object. Not a payload language.

adapters.description: Framework adapters. Opt-in and never discovered from a target repository: a manifest sitting in a checkout must not be able to cause a program to run. Adapters contribute expectations about what an application should enforce; whether it does is established by the runtime checks.

sourceRoot.description: The application source to inspect. Required when any adapter is configured.

trust.description: Defaults to none. "execute-target-code" authorises adapters that run the inspected application's own code — asking Laravel to list its routes boots the framework and runs every service provider, and importing a NestJS module executes it. Adapters reporting framework-native extraction are refused unless this is set.

name.description: Must match the name the adapter reports, so a document cannot be attributed to an adapter that did not produce it.

path.description: The adapter executable, run directly with an explicit argument vector and never through a shell.

passEnv.description: Environment variables to forward. The adapter's environment is otherwise built from nothing. This tool's own identity credentials can never be forwarded, whatever is named here.

engines.description: External scanning engines. Each is a known integration, not a command you compose: there is deliberately no command, args or env field, because those would make AppSec Framework a general process runner and turn its argument-vector construction, minimal environment and profile gating into things a configuration file could opt out of. An engine's results are recorded as observed and are never promoted to confirmed on the engine's own confidence.

sourceRoot.description: An application checkout, for engines that read code.

nuclei.description: Nuclei. Templates are executable security logic and must be supplied locally: AppSec Framework will not let Nuclei fetch its own, because a corpus that changed overnight makes results incomparable. Unsigned templates, code templates, headless browsing, redirect following, cloud upload and out-of-band interaction are all disabled.

enabled.description: Engines are off by default: none runs because it happens to be installed.

executable.description: Explicit path. Empty looks the engine's own binary name up on PATH.

passEnv.description: Variables to forward. The engine's environment is otherwise built from nothing, and this tool's identity credentials can never be forwarded.

severity.description: Optional severity filter, in the engine's own vocabulary.

templates.description: Local template directory. Required when nuclei is enabled. A git checkout is recorded by commit, which is what makes a run reproducible.

allowUnsignedTemplates.description: Execute templates that carry no Nuclei signature. Off by default. With it off, a corpus in which nothing is signed is refused rather than run, because Nuclei would exclude every template, exit successfully and produce a scan that reports no findings after checking nothing. Turning it on is a statement that you trust this directory: a template is executable security logic aimed at your own target, and the provenance of every resulting observation records that nothing else established it.

zap.description: ZAP, run one-shot rather than as a daemon, with a private home inside the run's workspace. It runs unauthenticated: AppSec Framework does not hand identity credentials to a third-party engine.

enabled.description: Engines are off by default: none runs because it happens to be installed.

executable.description: Explicit path. Empty looks the engine's own binary name up on PATH.

passEnv.description: Variables to forward. The engine's environment is otherwise built from nothing, and this tool's identity credentials can never be forwarded.

severity.description: Optional severity filter, in the engine's own vocabulary.

mode.description: Defaults to passive. "active" runs ZAP's active scanner, which sends attack payloads and therefore requires assessment.profile: intrusive. A passive run does not assess injection and does not claim to.

sast.description: Semgrep or opengrep. opengrep is preferred when both are installed: it is the fork without Semgrep's AUTO metrics default and without the registry rule licence. Rules must be local — a registry identifier would fetch over the network and, for Semgrep, enable telemetry. Source findings are observations, not evidence that anything is reachable at runtime.

enabled.description: Engines are off by default: none runs because it happens to be installed.

executable.description: Explicit path. Empty looks the engine's own binary name up on PATH.

passEnv.description: Variables to forward. The engine's environment is otherwise built from nothing, and this tool's identity credentials can never be forwarded.

severity.description: Optional severity filter, in the engine's own vocabulary.

rules.description: Local rule file or directory. Required when sast is enabled. AppSec Framework ships no rules.

openAPIFile.description: Path to a specification on disk. Empty means unset.

openAPIURL.description: URL of a specification served by the target. Empty means unset.

outcome.description: Application-specific signals for classifying responses. These come from the operator only: a target that could define its own oracle could suppress every finding.

errorCodePointer.description: JSON pointer to a stable machine-readable error code, e.g. "/errorCode".

environment.description: Stated deviations from production, recorded as facts. AppSec Framework does not compute a fidelity score.

policy.description: When a run fails the build. Severity thresholds; empty disables a rule. Suspected findings count by default, because AppSec Framework cannot reach 'confirmed' without credentials and gating only on confirmed findings would exit 0 on a real bypass.

failOnConfirmed.description: Lowest severity of a CONFIRMED finding that fails the run.

failOnSuspected.description: Lowest severity of a SUSPECTED finding that fails the run.
